title: Grade 8 Science — Wed, Jun 03
description: Synthetic Fibres & Plastics — Day 3 of 5: Plastics and their properties
subject: science

questions.question: Plastic is also a polymer. Plastics that can be moulded again and again on heating are called:
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics can be softened by heating and moulded repeatedly, like polythene and PVC.

questions.question: Plastics that, once moulded and set, cannot be softened again by heating are called:
questions.explanation: Thermosetting plastics, like bakelite and melamine, cannot be remoulded once set.

questions.question: Which is an example of a thermoplastic?
questions.explanation: Polythene and PVC are thermoplastics that can be remoulded on heating.

questions.question: Bakelite is used for electrical switches and plug handles because it is a:
options: Good conductor of heat and electricity
Poor conductor of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Bakelite is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, making it safe for electrical fittings.

questions.question: Melamine is used to make floor tiles and unbreakable kitchenware because it:
options: Resists fire and can tolerate heat
questions.explanation: Melamine resists fire and tolerates heat, so it is used for kitchenware and fire-resistant fabrics.

questions.question: Plastic is widely used for storing food and chemicals because it is:
options: Non-reactive and does not react with air, water or many chemicals
questions.explanation: Plastic is non-reactive, so it does not corrode or react with stored substances.

questions.question: Plastic is preferred for many containers because it is light, strong and:
questions.explanation: Plastic is cheap, light, strong and durable, making it useful for many products.

questions.question: Why are cooking pan handles often made of plastic?
options: Plastic is a good conductor of heat
Plastic is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle stays cool
questions.explanation: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle does not get too hot to hold.

questions.question: Teflon, a special plastic that food does not stick to, is used to coat:
questions.explanation: Teflon is used to coat non-stick pans because food and oil do not stick to it.

questions.question: Plastic does not react with water, so it is useful but also a problem because it:
options: Does not decompose easily and causes pollution
questions.explanation: Because plastic does not rot or decompose easily, waste plastic remains for years and pollutes.

questions.question: A material that can be broken down by natural processes is called:
questions.explanation: Biodegradable materials are broken down by bacteria and other natural processes.

questions.question: Plastic is an example of a ____ material.
questions.explanation: Plastic is non-biodegradable; it is not easily broken down by natural processes.

questions.question: Which use matches the correct property of plastic?
options: Plastic raincoat – because it absorbs water
Plastic electrical socket – because it does not conduct electricity
Plastic pan base – because it conducts heat
questions.explanation: Plastic does not conduct electricity, so it is safe for electrical sockets and switches.

questions.question: How does a thermosetting plastic differ from a thermoplastic?
options: A thermoplastic cannot be remoulded; a thermosetting plastic can
A thermosetting plastic cannot be remoulded once set; a thermoplastic can
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics can be remoulded by heating; thermosetting plastics set permanently.

questions.question: The very property that makes plastic useful — being unreactive and long-lasting — is also why it:
options: Stays in the environment for a very long time
questions.explanation: Because plastic is unreactive and durable, it persists in the environment and is hard to dispose of.
